correctness.rationale: For any real eigenvalue with z nonzero in ker(Cbar), the first and third normalized block equations give x* Atilde x=lambda(||x||^2+||z||^2); x is nonzero since Bbar has full row rank, so 0<lambda<b. Only if lambda<a is Atilde-lambda I SPD and its inverse >= (b-lambda)^{-1} I; this yields lambda(b-lambda)>=beta. The quadratic-root case split proves the clipped floor without assuming invertibility of Etilde-lambda I. For every t>=1 the constructed blocks are SPD/full rank, yield an exact eigenpair lambda=1, z in ker(C), with beta/b=(3+7t^2)/7 unbounded; an exact low-coupling equality instance is supplied. Packaged Python Fraction verifier checks two rational points t=1,11 and the sharp instance; the continuum and universal theorem rest on algebra, not finite computations.

value.rationale: The motivating PDE-constrained numerical-linear-algebra spectral lemma supplies an allegedly uniform positive eigenvalue enclosure. Keeping A and E spectra and their condition numbers fixed while the asserted floor diverges exposes a meaningful structural failure not explained by singular diagonal blocks or a limit on their conditioning. The corrected conditional resolvent enclosure is a usable mathematical repair, with exact root equality on a natural branch. This is relevant to reliability of preconditioner spectral predictions, not a fabricated application claim. The proof avoids alleging invalidity of unrelated main theorems or numerical experiments.
